Class LeaderboardController

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.client.ui.gui.LeaderboardController
public class LeaderboardController extends Object
JavaFX controller for the end-game leaderboard screen (leaderboardBoard.fxml).

The screen has two views that are swapped at runtime:

  • Match ranking (rankingTable) — shown immediately on load; lists all players sorted by prestige points (descending), with food as a tiebreaker. The local player's row is highlighted in gold.
  • Global leaderboard (globalTable) — revealed when the player clicks the "Global Leaderboard" button; shows cumulative points across all recorded matches of the same player count, fetched from the server's PostgreSQL database. If the database is unreachable, a fallback message is shown in txtPlayerRank instead.

All methods that touch JavaFX nodes are guarded by assertFxThread(). Network requests (quit, ranking fetch) are dispatched on short-lived daemon threads to keep the FX Application Thread free.

  • Method Details

    • initialize

      public void initialize()
      Called automatically by the FXMLLoader after all @FXML fields have been injected.

      Configures both tables to use a constrained column-resize policy and wires their cell-value factories:

      • colPos — derived from the row's index in the sorted items list (1-based).
      • colNickname, colPP, colFood — mapped directly from the corresponding PlayerStatsDTO fields.
      • globalColPos — computed with dense ranking: iterates the global table items and assigns the same rank to entries with equal point totals.
      • globalColNickname, globalColPoints — mapped from the Map.Entry key and value respectively.

      The global table is initially hidden and unmanaged; it is revealed when the player clicks the global-leaderboard button.

    • setData

      public void setData(List<PlayerStatsDTO> stats, int myRankingPos, ViewGUI viewGUI, int globalRankingPos)
      Populates the match-ranking table and configures the global-ranking status label.

      Players are sorted by prestige points descending, with remaining food as a tiebreaker. The table height is capped at five visible rows (45 px each, plus a 30 px header). A custom TableRow factory highlights the local player's row with a translucent gold background (rgba(255,215,0,0.35)).

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

      Parameters:
      stats - final stats for all players in the match
      myRankingPos - the local player's 1-based finishing position; used to identify the row to highlight
      viewGUI - the owning view, stored for later client access
      globalRankingPos - the local player's position in the persistent global leaderboard for this player count, or -1 if the database was unreachable

    • onMainMenu

      public void onMainMenu()
      Handles the "Main Menu" button click: dispatches a ClientToServerActions.quit() call on a background thread, which causes the server to clean up the session and the client to navigate back to the main-menu scene.

    • onGlobalLeaderboard

      public void onGlobalLeaderboard()
      Handles the "Global Leaderboard" button click: requests the persistent ranking from the server on a background thread.

      When the server responds, it calls showGlobalRanking(Map) on the FX Application Thread to populate and reveal globalTable.

    • showGlobalRanking

      public void showGlobalRanking(Map<String,Integer> ranks)
      Populates and reveals the global-leaderboard table with the ranking data received from the server.

      Entries are sorted by cumulative points descending, with the nickname as an alphabetical tiebreaker. The table height is capped at eight visible rows. A custom TableRow factory applies the CSS class my-row to the entry that matches the local player's nickname.

      Once the global table is shown, rankingTable and globalLeaderboardBtn are hidden and unmanaged to keep the layout clean, while backToMatchBtn is revealed so the player can return to the match ranking via onBackToMatchRanking().

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

      Parameters:
      ranks - map from player nickname to their cumulative point total in the global leaderboard for this match's player count

    • onBackToMatchRanking

      public void onBackToMatchRanking()
      Handles the "Indietro" button click: hides the global leaderboard view and brings back the end-of-match ranking view, restoring the "Classifica globale" button so the global ranking can be reopened.

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread (it is triggered directly by a button click on that thread).
